Calculate a self-reported multimorbidity index

Source: R/multimorbidity_index.R
multimorbidity_index.Rd

Computes an individual-level multimorbidity score from a set of self-reported binary condition indicators (e.g. "Has a doctor ever told you that you have hypertension?"). This is designed for population health survey data (WHO STEPS, DHS, SAGE, etc.), where multimorbidity is captured through self-report rather than ICD-coded diagnoses – a data shape that existing comorbidity packages (which all assume ICD claims data) don't handle.

Usage

multimorbidity_index(
  data,
  conditions,
  weights = NULL,
  na_action = c("ignore", "na"),
  threshold = 2
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per individual.

conditions

A character vector of column names in data. Each column must already be coded 0/1/NA (1 = condition present). Use recode_binary() first if your raw data uses Yes/No, 1/2, etc.

weights

Optional named numeric vector giving a weight for each condition (names must match conditions). If NULL (the default), every condition counts equally – i.e. a simple unweighted sum, which is how the published Functional Comorbidity Index (Groll et al. 2005) is scored. See fci_items().

na_action

How to handle a row with at least one missing condition. "ignore" (default) sums whatever conditions are non-missing for that person. "na" returns NA for that person's index entirely, which is the safer choice once you move to population-level (survey-weighted) estimates, since silently treating missing as absent can bias prevalence downward.

threshold

Number of conditions at or above which a respondent is classified as multimorbid. The default, 2, is the most common definition; 3 is often used for "complex multimorbidity".

Value

data with four columns appended: mm_n_conditions (raw count of conditions present), mm_index (the possibly weighted score), mm_category (factor: "None", "Single condition" or, when threshold > 2, "1-k conditions", and "Multimorbid") and mm_multimorbid (1 if the count is at least threshold, else 0).

References

Groll, D. L., To, T., Bombardier, C., & Wright, J. G. (2005). The development of a comorbidity index with physical function as the outcome. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 58(6), 595-602. doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2004.10.018

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  id           = 1:5,
  hypertension = c(1, 0, 1, 1, 0),
  diabetes     = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0),
  arthritis    = c(1, 0, 0, 1, NA)
)
multimorbidity_index(df, conditions = c("hypertension", "diabetes", "arthritis"))
#>   id hypertension diabetes arthritis mm_n_conditions mm_index mm_category
#> 1  1            1        0         1               2        2 Multimorbid
#> 2  2            0        0         0               0        0        None
#> 3  3            1        1         0               2        2 Multimorbid
#> 4  4            1        1         1               3        3 Multimorbid
#> 5  5            0        0        NA               0        0        None
#>   mm_multimorbid
#> 1              1
#> 2              0
#> 3              1
#> 4              1
#> 5              0
